<div class="abstract-section">
  <div class="abstract-content">
    <p>Machine learning has evolved from a research discipline into an engineering practice. Building systems that learn from data requires more than understanding algorithms—it demands expertise spanning data pipelines, model development, optimization for deployment constraints, and operational practices. This book introduces AI engineering: the discipline of building ML systems that work in the real world. The treatment covers four areas: foundations (system characteristics, development workflows), building (deep learning mathematics, architectures, framework internals), optimization (compression, hardware acceleration, benchmarking), and deployment (serving infrastructure, operations, responsible engineering). The emphasis throughout is on engineering trade-offs and quantitative analysis.</p>
  </div>

<h2>What You Will Learn</h2>

<p>The book progresses through four stages:</p>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Part I: Foundations</strong>—Build your conceptual foundation with mental models that underpin all effective systems work.</li>
  <li><strong>Part II: Build</strong>—Engineer complete workflows from data pipelines through training infrastructure.</li>
  <li><strong>Part III: Optimize</strong>—Transform theoretical understanding into systems that run efficiently in resource-constrained environments.</li>
  <li><strong>Part IV: Deploy</strong>—Navigate serving, operations, and responsible engineering practices.</li>
</ul>

<h2>Prerequisites</h2>

<p>This book assumes:</p>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Programming proficiency</strong> in Python with familiarity in NumPy</li>
  <li><strong>Mathematics foundations</strong> in linear algebra, calculus, and probability at the undergraduate level</li>
  <li>Prior ML experience is helpful but not required; neural computation provides essential background</li>
</ul>

<h2>Learn by Doing</h2>

<p>Beyond the chapters, this volume is the reading spine for a broader AI engineering curriculum. Pair the chapters with <a href="https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/">Co-Labs</a> to test predictions, <a href="https://mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch/">TinyTorch</a> to build framework internals, <a href="https://mlsysbook.ai/mlsysim/">MLSys·im</a> to model hardware constraints, and <a href="https://mlsysbook.ai/kits/">Hardware Kits</a> to deploy on real devices. Instructors can adopt the full sequence through <a href="https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/">The AI Engineering Blueprint</a>.</p>

async function fetchGitHubStars() {
  const starElement = document.getElementById('star-count');

    const formattedCount = starCount.toLocaleString();
    starElement.textContent = formattedCount;
    starElement.style.opacity = '1';
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to fetch GitHub stars:', error);
    starElement.textContent = 'Loading...';
    starElement.style.opacity = '1';

}
